newsitem.title: USA: World electricity use to rise 2.8 pct annually-EIA.
newsitem.headline: World electricity use to rise 2.8 pct annually-EIA.

text.p: The world's total annual electricity demand should nearly double between 1995 and 2015, with about half the increase coming from the developing world, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said Tuesday.

With demand expected to increase more rapidly for electricity than any other form of energy, the EIA said worldwide consumption should increase 2.8 percent annually to 20.0 trillion kilowatthours in 2015 from 1995's 11.44 trillion kilowatthours.
In its international outlook, the EIA said demand in developing countries should increase 4.6 percent annually to 7.26 trillion kilowatthours in 2015 from 2.96 trillion in 1995.
In industrialized countries, electricity use should rise by 2.2 percent annually to 10.67 trillion kilowatthours in 2015 from 6.95 trillion in 1995.
Growth in the United States should be at a 1.5 percent annual rate to 4.04 trillion kilowatthours in 2015 from 3.01 trillion in 1995.
The Former Soviet Union and Eastern Europe also should have a 1.5 percent annual growth rate to 2.07 trillion kilowatthours in 2015 from 1.53 trillion.
